commit_message: avcodec/exr: use tile dimensions in pxr24 UINT case
vulnerability_type: Out-of-bounds read/write in EXR pxr24 UINT decompression due to incorrect tile dimension variable
poc_sketch: Craft a tiled EXR file with PXR24 compression containing a UINT channel where tile dimensions (td->xsize) differ from s->xdelta, causing buffer overread/overwrite during decompression of the UINT pixel data path
backport_notes: Patch replaces 5 instances of s->xdelta with td->xsize in the EXR_UINT case block. Pure variable name substitution with no structural changes, no new dependencies, no API changes.
logical_survival: The vulnerable code is core EXR decoder tile-handling logic that is algorithmically stable across versions; the patch is fully decoupled from version-specific features and fixes a straightforward variable reference bug.
ubuntu_2604_evidence: Manual backport / Debian-layer patch (author: veyga@veygax.dev). upstream: avcodec/exr: use tile dimensions in pxr24 UINT case
_cot_rationale: The Ubuntu 24.04 source at lines 686-693 shows expected_len calculated using td->xsize*td->ysize, and the FLOAT/HALF cases correctly use td->xsize for pointer arithmetic and loop bounds. However, the EXR_UINT case (not shown in 24.04 excerpt but confirmed present via the patch diff context) uses s->xdelta instead of td->xsize for both pointer stride calculations and loop iteration count. When s->xdelta != td->xsize (possible with tiled EXR where tile dimensions differ from overall image scanline width), this creates a mismatch: the decompressed buffer is sized for td->xsize bytes per row but the UINT path reads/writes s->xdelta bytes per row. If s->xdelta > td->xsize, this causes heap buffer overread (reading past decompressed data) and overwrite (writing past destination buffer). The patch is a minimal 5-line variable name change with zero structural impact, making backport trivial. Severity is HIGH because EXR is a commonly-used format, tiled EXR with PXR24 compression and UINT channels is a realistic combination, and the memory corruption is attacker-controllable through crafted tile dimension parameters.

commit_message: x509/name_constraints: make types_with_empty_intersection a bitmask
vulnerability_type: Logic error in X.509 name constraints intersection causing incorrect tracking of empty intersection per type, leading to missing universal excluded constraints

When the intersection of permitted subtrees becomes empty for a specific type, the buggy array-based tracking may fail to correctly record or propagate this state due to type-indexing inconsistencies. The only prerequisite is verifying that GNUTLS_SAN_MAX < 8 in the 3.8.3 codebase (which it is, since GnuTLS SAN type enums are small). No new APIs, no cross-file dependencies, no structural changes to adjacent code.
logical_survival: The name_constraints intersection logic is stable core X.509 validation code that has not undergone major restructuring across GnuTLS 3.8.x releases, and the patch is fully decoupled from version-specific features—it only refactors internal bookkeeping within a single static function.

commit_message: buffer: add more extensive integer overflow checks
vulnerability_type: Integer overflow in buffer resize operations leading to heap buffer overflow
poc_sketch: An attacker crafts a TLS handshake or certificate that causes gnutls_buffer_append_data to be called with a data_size near SIZE_MAX minus dest->length. On line 104, the addition overflows, producing a small tot_len. The flawed 32-bit-only check (lines 113-117) passes on 64-bit systems and uses incorrect ssize_t casts. _gnutls_buffer_resize allocates a tiny buffer, then memcpy at line 125 writes far beyond allocated memory, corrupting heap metadata and potentially enabling RCE.
backport_notes: The gnutls_buffer_append_data fix is straightforward — replace the flawed conditional overflow check with INT_ADD_OK. However, the resize functions were refactored upstream into buffer_resize_no_reclaim and buffer_resize_reclaim, while 24.04 has a single _gnutls_buffer_resize with #ifdef AGGRESSIVE_REALLOC paths. Each resize variant in 24.04 must be individually identified and patched with equivalent INT_ADD_OK guards. Requires verifying INT_ADD_OK macro availability in 3.8.3.
logical_survival: The buffer append/resize logic is foundational GnuTLS infrastructure used across TLS operations; it is highly stable core code unlikely to have been restructured within 24.04's lifecycle, and the patch addresses a generic algorithmic overflow bug fully decoupled from any version-specific API changes.

_cot_rationale: The 24.04 code at line 104 computes tot_len = data_size + dest->length unconditionally before any check, enabling integer overflow. The existing guard (lines 113-117) is deficient: (1) it only activates on 32-bit (sizeof(size_t)==4), leaving 64-bit systems unprotected; (2) it casts to ssize_t which itself overflows for values > SSIZE_MAX; (3) it checks MAX(data_size, MIN_CHUNK) rather than the actual data_size. The upstream patch replaces all of this with a single correct INT_ADD_OK that works on all platforms and atomically checks-and-computes. Additionally, the resize helper functions have their own unchecked additions (new_size + unused, and the alloc_len computation in reclaim path) that are also fixed by the patch. The core vulnerability in gnutls_buffer_append_data is directly applicable; the resize function fixes require adaptation since upstream refactored into separate reclaim/no-reclaim functions while 24.04 uses a different code structure with #ifdef AGGRESSIVE_REALLOC.

commit_message: ICU-22775 fix StringSearch pattern CE mem mgmt
vulnerability_type: Heap buffer overflow in StringSearch pattern CE table due to missing bounds check on null terminator write and flawed reallocation logic
poc_sketch: Craft a Unicode pattern string that produces collation elements filling the CE array to exactly its capacity. When initializePatternCETable writes the null terminator at cetable[offset] = 0 (line 317), it writes one past the allocated buffer. Alternatively, if the reallocation condition offset+1==newlength is bypassed (offset jumps past), out-of-bounds writes occur during the loop. Trigger via usearch_open followed by usearch_search with attacker-controlled pattern text.
backport_notes: The patch changes function signatures of addTouint32_tArray and addTouint64_tArray (adds destinationCapacity and destOnHeap params, reorders parameters), removes allocateMemory helper, and refactors caller logic in initializePatternCETable and initializePatternPCETable. All changes are in a single file (usearch.cpp) but require careful adaptation of function signatures, call sites, and memory ownership tracking. The destOnHeap flag consolidation simplifies the caller but changes the freeing responsibility model.
logical_survival: The vulnerable code is foundational ICU collation/string-search logic that rarely changes between versions, and the fix addresses a generic memory-management algorithmic flaw (off-by-one reallocation + unguarded terminator write) fully decoupled from any version-specific API or feature.
ubuntu_2604_evidence: Reachable from upstream tag release-78.2; arrived via natural version import. upstream: ICU-22775 fix StringSearch pattern CE mem mgmt
_cot_rationale: The 24.04 code at lines 298-319 shows the vulnerable pattern: addTouint32_tArray only reallocates when offset+1==newlength (exact equality, not >=), and critically, the null terminator cetable[offset]=0 at line 317 is written unconditionally after the loop without verifying array capacity. The patch fixes both issues: (1) changes reallocation condition to offset >= *destinationCapacity, (2) writes the terminator through addTouint32_tArray itself ensuring space exists, (3) consolidates memory ownership via destOnHeap flag eliminating error-prone manual freeing in callers. This is clearly present in 24.04's version 74.2 and absent per the patch in 26.04's version 78.2. Backport requires adapting both helper function signatures and two caller functions, but everything is self-contained in one file with no cross-file dependencies.
